headline: An 8-week routine with 2% Alpha Arbutin
footnote: 93% subjects said it reduced sun tanning after 4 weeks of use. 90% subjects noticed reduction in hyperpigmentation marks in 8 weeks. Frames are AI illustrations, not real results.
layout_description: Headline across the top; three equal portrait frames left to right (Day 1 / Week 4 / Week 8), each with a dark label bar along its bottom edge, showing AI-generated illustrations of the same cheek area (frames_prompt); AI-GENERATED — ILLUSTRATIVE mark top-right; small real pack shot bottom-right; study/qualifier footnote across the bottom band; CTA bottom-left.
image_prompt: Empty background scene only: an off-white seamless paper backdrop with a faint warm-grey gradient from top to bottom and a soft diagonal shadow from a window frame in the upper-left corner. Off-white, soft natural light, few props, clinical minimal style. Square 1080x1080. Keep the whole central band of the frame as an empty clear space, evenly lit and calm, reserved for three image panels and copy placed later, and keep the lower right corner empty for a pack photo. No product, no bottle, no packaging, no text, no letters, no logos, no people, no faces, no skin, no hands.
photography_needed: Real, consented, unretouched progress photos of the same person at Day 1, Week 4 and Week 8 from the brand's own consumer study (F24, F22), same framing, distance and light, with the study report on file, to replace the AI frames before any use.
adaptation_notes: Kept: three equal labelled progress frames (Chemist at Play, Re'equil), a footnote that carries the study qualifier (Chemist at Play) and a timeframe-led headline used as routine length, not a result (Dr. Sheth's). Frame labels use only page-stated timeframes: Week 4 (F24, tanning perception) and Week 8 (F22, marks perception); Day 1 is the start. Both stats stay perception stats with their qualifier in the footnote. Dropped: 'fades dark spots in 15 days' result headline, Dermat/clinically-certified badges, struck price, before/after wording, the benchmark comparison (F13) and melanin wording (F6, F26). Frames are AI illustrations: Severe, not exportable until real study photos replace them. RATING not added: the footnote is full with the two study lines.

blend_sources.took: footnote carrying the study qualifier under labelled frames
timeframe-led headline, used as routine length not a result

frames_prompt: Three side-by-side portrait panels of the same adult's cheek and cheekbone area (a woman in her late 20s with medium-brown skin), identical framing, camera distance, soft diffuse daylight from the upper left and a plain off-white backdrop in every panel, natural skin texture and visible pores throughout. Panel 1 (Day 1) shows a few small, faint, uneven-toned dark marks on the cheek; panel 2 (Week 4) shows the same area with a slightly softer tan tone; panel 3 (Week 8) shows the same marks looking slightly less visible. Changes are small, subtle and realistic, never dramatic, with no retouching gloss, makeup or jewellery. No product, no bottle, no packaging, no hands, no text, no letters, no logos.

verdict.label: Fix before review
verdict.detail: Change the flagged lines, or attach the substantiation a reviewer would need to accept them.

findings.message: The Day 1 / Week 4 / Week 8 frames, matched to the 4- and 8-week stats, form a before/after progression, and AI-generated frames are not representative, unretouched evidence (the "not real results" note sits only in the footnote). If the frames show skin getting lighter overall rather than dark spots fading, it also drifts toward CLM-06.
findings.fix: Relabel the frames as routine stages (e.g. "Week 8 · in the routine") with the AI-illustration note on the image itself, or replace them with real, unretouched study photos and their qualifier.

findings.message: Statistics need their study qualifier on the creative and must not be worded more strongly than the study.
findings.fix: Quote the stat exactly as the study states it ('90% subjects said…') and add a footnote: study type (consumer perception / in-vivo / in-vitro), duration, and n if known.
findings.note: Wording appears on the product page (F24). Severity lowered one step: the brand has published it, but a reviewer must still confirm substantiation is on file.

findings.message: A time-bound result needs a study of that duration, with the qualifier shown on the creative.
findings.fix: Keep the timeframe only if it comes from a study you can cite, and put the qualifier in the footnote (e.g. '*Consumer perception study, 4 weeks'). Otherwise remove the timeframe.
